item.research_question: Can a high-entropy glass system (HEGS) doped with neodymium ions exhibit spatially coherent radiation without a common nonlinear optical process?
item.processing_route: The HEGS was prepared by melting a mixture of Zn(H2PO4)2·2H2O, P2O5, TEOS, K2SO4, NdCl3·6H2O, LiOH·H2O, and CaCl2 at 700 °C and then annealing the sample
item.test_conditions: The emission spectra were measured using a fiber optic spectrometer, and the spatial coherence was measured by placing the fiber port on a circle of radius 20 mm centered on the midpoint of the sample rod
key_findings: The HEGS exhibits a much broader infrared absorption than common glass systems
The BPAWR-SACM process has a low threshold and can be controlled by changing excitation wavelengths, sample size, and doping concentrations
The time delay between the pump pulse and the BPAWR-SACM signal is 1.66 ns, which is much longer than the Raman process
The BPAWR-SACM process can amplify the centered non-absorption band with a gain up to 26.02 dB

The area ratio of red-shifted to blue-shifted BPAWR-SACM signal at different excitation wavelengths is positively correlated with the absorption peak area-ratio between adjacent higher excited state and lower excited state
item.mechanism: The BPAWR-SACM process consists of a broadened-phonon-assisted wideband radiation (BPAWR) process and a subsequent self-absorption coherence modulation (SACM) process
item.limitations: The conversion efficiency of the BPAWR-SACM process is low, and the output power is weak
item.future_work: Investigating the application of the BPAWR-SACM process in supercontinuum, laser amplification, and optical communication
quotes: the spatially coherent radiation within a certain frequency range can be obtained without a common nonlinear optical process

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a high-entropy glass system (HEGS) doped with neodymium ions exhibit spatially coherent radiation without a common nonlinear optical process?. System: Nd3+-doped high entropy glass system (HEGS). Processing: The HEGS was prepared by melting a mixture of Zn(H2PO4)2·2H2O, P2O5, TEOS, K2SO4, NdCl3·6H2O, LiOH·H2O, and CaCl2 at 700 °C and then annealing the sample. Test conditions: The emission spectra were measured using a fiber optic spectrometer, and the spatial coherence was measured by placing the fiber port on a circle of radius 20 mm centered on the midpoint of the sample rod. Findings: The HEGS exhibits a much broader infrared absorption than common glass systems; The BPAWR-SACM process has a low threshold and can be controlled by changing excitation wavelengths, sample size, and doping concentrations; The time delay between the pump pulse and the BPAWR-SACM signal is 1.66 ns, which is much longer than the Raman process; The BPAWR-SACM process can amplify the centered non-absorption band with a gain up to 26.02 dB; The area ratio of red-shifted to blue-shifted BPAWR-SACM signal at different excitation wavelengths is positively correlated with the absorption peak area-ratio between adjacent higher excited state and lower excited state. Mechanism: The BPAWR-SACM process consists of a broadened-phonon-assisted wideband radiation (BPAWR) process and a subsequent self-absorption coherence modulation (SACM) process. Limitations: The conversion efficiency of the BPAWR-SACM process is low, and the output power is weak. Future work: Investigating the application of the BPAWR-SACM process in supercontinuum, laser amplification, and optical communication. Quote: "the spatially coherent radiation within a certain frequency range can be obtained without a common nonlinear optical process"
